subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — VectorFin reserved pool fit check
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Michael Liu <michael.liu@vectorfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — VectorFin reserved pool fit check

Hi Michael — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we all have the same view.

Summary of pain and goals (as we heard them)
- Primary pain: production inference cost variability and noisy multi-tenant interference impacting 95th percentile latency for customer-facing scoring endpoints.
- Business goal: consistent latency and predictable cost for the fraud-scoring path used in pre-auth flows.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 150ms at peak traffic, predictable monthly inference cost +/-10%, and data isolation for PCI-adjacent signals.

Current stack (what you said)
- Inference: on-prem model serving today for batch scoring; moving customer-facing scoring to cloud in next 6–9 months.
- Models: ensemble of a distilled transformer + lightweight logistic scorer; typical context length small (~512 tokens) but traffic spikes around payroll cycles.
- Data/security: KMS-managed keys, SOC2 in progress, need VPC-level isolation for the inference tier.

Prelim Dedicated fit assessment (items to validate)
- Target steady TPS: ~120 TPS average during business hours; peak burst up to ~300 TPS for 10–30 minute windows.
- Isolation: must run in a reserved pool (no noisy neighbors), customer VPC or private deployment acceptable.
- Autoscale/burst: want deterministic burst capacity (2–3x baseline) with a cap and predictable billing.
- Latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms for the primary scoring path.

Immediate next steps (owners in parentheses):
1) We will share a short reserved-pool checklist and a preliminary cost model (attached). (Evelyn)
2) Can you confirm average TPS and peak burst windows and share any historical traffic traces you can (safest with anonymization)? (Michael/VectorFin)
3) Steph/Ben — follow up with a short note on our typical reserved pool sizing and the autoscaling policy options we recommend. (Ben/Steph)
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/SRE folks to validate network/KMS requirements and run a quick throughput baseline. (All)

Attachments: vectorfin-prelim-cost-model.xlsx (cost sketch), redwood-dedicated-fit-checklist.pdf (short checklist).

Proposed times for deep-dive next week: Tue 12:00–13:00 PST or Wed 08:00–09:00 PST. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Liu <michael.liu@vectorfin.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@vectorfin.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — VectorFin reserved pool fit check

Evelyn — thanks for the thorough recap. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) TPS: our telemetry team reports ~110 TPS avg for the scoring endpoint; the 300 TPS peak is accurate but typically lasts ~15 minutes and happens 2–3 times per month. We can share anonymized logs for a 30-day window.
2) Isolation: we must run in a dedicated environment; a VPC-hosted dedicated pool is preferred. On-prem is possible but we want cloud first.
3) Security: SOC2 Type II audit is scheduled Q1; we need to ensure KMS integration and retention controls.

Next steps for us — we’ll: 
- Export the 30-day anonymized trace and drop it to the link you share (Michael).
- Procurement prep: I CC’d procurement; they’ll review the attachments and come back with a standard PO / MSA question list.

Tue 12:00 PST works for the deep-dive — please send invite. Also curious: do you have a short runbook for failure modes (what happens if a pool is saturated)? That’ll help us evaluate fallback options.

Thanks,
Michael
VP Engineering — VectorFin
michael.liu@vectorfin.com | +1 (617) 555-9876

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — VectorFin reserved pool fit check

Eve — quick internal note before the deep-dive.

- I’ll draft a 1-page reserved-pool sizing note based on 120 TPS steady / 300 TPS burst — thinking a 4x A100 equivalent reserved pool with a burst buffer of 2 extra nodes to hit 300 TPS while keeping p95 under 150ms. I’ll include cost delta between strict reservation vs. reservation + burst credit.
- Steph, can you pull recent examples of our autoscale policy configs and the failure-mode runbook Michael asked about? I’ve seen the runbook used in two enterprise pilots; we should customize for VectorFin’s retention/KMS constraints.

I’ll loop back with the draft by 11:30 PST so Eve can include it in the deep-dive.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

- 12:30–12:45 — Security/KMS & VPC integration checks (owner: Stephanie)
- 12:45–13:00 — Validation items and next steps / procurement timeline (owner: Evelyn)

Prep for VectorFin — please upload the anonymized 30-day trace to the HubSpot file link or reply with a Drive link (we’ll only use it for baseline sizing). Procurement, feel free to add PO/MSA questions ahead of the call and we’ll have legal ready to respond.

Calendar invite sent. If anything changes, let me know. Talk tomorrow.
